PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Truthfulness means telling the truth always, whatever the results may be. In this sub-strand you will learn why telling the truth is important, what Proverbs 12:19 teaches about lies, and how Ephesians 4:25 calls Christians to speak the truth to one another.

## Strand 4.0: Christian Values
Sub-strand 4.2: Truthfulness
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) state the importance of telling the truth
b) resist lying as cited in Proverbs 12:19
c) desire to always speak the truth according to Ephesians 4:25

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why should you always tell the truth?

## Core competencies
• Imagination and Creativity: the skill of coming up with new ideas and originality is enhanced as they write a poem on the importance of always telling the truth.
• Communication and collaboration: the skill of speaking clearly and effectively is enhanced as learners, in pairs, say when they did not tell the truth and how to overcome lies.

## Values
• Integrity: learners say why they should always tell the truth.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Social Cohesion is portrayed as learners resist lying by always telling the truth.

## Links to other learning areas
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners write a poem.
• English: speaking skills are enhanced as learners read and recite Bible texts.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 4.0 Christian Values, Sub-strand 4.2 Truthfulness
• Proverbs 12:19; Ephesians 4:25 (Good News Bible)
• KICD Grade 4 CRE radio programme 14 (Truthfulness)

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Why we should tell the truth

LESSON 1: WHY WE SHOULD TELL THE TRUTH
======================================

## What you will learn
• Explain what truthfulness means.
• State the importance of telling the truth.

Curriculum outcomes: a) state the importance of telling the truth

## Introduction
A learner breaks a window while playing football. The teacher asks who did it. Should the learner speak up, or keep quiet and let someone else be blamed?

## Notes
### What is truthfulness?
Truthfulness is telling the truth always, no matter what the results are. A truthful person says what really happened, does not add or hide facts to deceive others, and keeps promises.

A lie is saying something you know is not true so that others believe it. Lying can also happen when we keep quiet and allow someone else to be blamed, or when we tell only part of the story so as to mislead.

### Why should we tell the truth?
- God commands it. God is truthful, and He wants His children to be truthful too.
- Other people trust us. Parents, teachers and friends believe what a truthful person says.
- It helps us make and keep friends. Friends stay close to someone they can depend on.
- We have peace in our hearts. A person who lies worries about being found out.
- Lies are found out in the end. One lie often needs another lie to cover it, until the truth comes out.
- It protects innocent people. When we tell the truth, others are not punished for what we did.
- It helps problems to be solved. A doctor can treat you well only if you say truthfully how you feel; a teacher can help you only if you say truthfully what you did not understand.

### Back to the broken window
If the learner owns up and says sorry, the teacher knows what happened, nobody else is punished, and the learner keeps a clean heart. The learner may still need to help repair the window, but people will trust him or her more in future.

Telling the truth sometimes needs courage. Christians can pray and ask God for the courage to be honest.

## Key words
• truthfulness — telling the truth always
• lie — something said to make others believe what is not true
• integrity — being honest and doing right even when it is hard

## Activity: Why tell the truth?
You will need: Chalkboard or manila paper, Exercise book
1. In groups, say why you should always tell the truth and list your reasons.
2. Each group reads its list to the class; the class makes one combined list.
3. Each learner copies the list and underlines the reason he or she thinks is most important.

## Practice
1. What is truthfulness?
2. Give three reasons why we should tell the truth.
3. Is keeping quiet while a friend is punished for your mistake a lie? Explain.

## Summary
• Truthfulness is telling the truth always.
• Telling the truth pleases God, builds trust and gives peace.
• Lies are found out in the end.

### Answers to practice
1. Telling the truth always, no matter what the results are.
2. Any three: God commands it; people trust us; we keep friends; we have peace; lies are found out; innocent people are not punished.
3. Yes. You allow others to believe something untrue, so it deceives them.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Resisting lies: Proverbs 12:19

LESSON 2: RESISTING LIES: PROVERBS 12:19
========================================

## What you will learn
• Recite Proverbs 12:19.
• Describe situations where people are tempted to lie and how to overcome lies.

Curriculum outcomes: b) resist lying as cited in Proverbs 12:19

## Introduction
Some people think a small lie will get them out of trouble quickly. The Bible shows that a lie does not last, but the truth does.

## Notes
### Proverbs 12:19
The Good News Bible says:

"A lie has a short life, but truth lives on forever."

This means a lie may seem to help for a short time, but it is soon found out and forgotten. The truth stays true and continues to stand.

### When are people tempted to lie?
- To escape punishment, for example after breaking something or coming home late.
- To get something, such as saying the school asked for money when it did not.
- To look important in front of friends.
- To avoid work, such as saying "I have finished my homework" when you have not.
- Out of fear, when we think the truth will make someone angry.

### What happens when we lie?
- We lose the trust of others. Even when we later tell the truth, people may not believe us.
- We may need more lies to cover the first one.
- Other people may be hurt or punished wrongly.
- We feel guilty and lose our peace.
- Most importantly, lying is sin; it does not please God.

### How to overcome lies
- Stop and think before you speak.
- Remember that God sees everything.
- Own up quickly when you do wrong, and say sorry.
- Ask God in prayer for courage to tell the truth.
- Choose friends who tell the truth.
- If you have lied, go back and correct it. Say, "What I told you was not true. This is what happened."

### Example
Otieno lost the money his mother gave him for bread because he was playing on the way. He is tempted to say that someone stole it. Instead, he tells his mother the truth and says sorry. His mother is disappointed, but she forgives him and knows she can believe him.

## Key words
• resist — to refuse to give in to something
• guilty — feeling bad inside because you did wrong
• own up — to admit that you did something wrong

## Activity: Flash cards and sharing
You will need: Flash cards, Markers or crayons
1. Write Proverbs 12:19 on a flash card and decorate it.
2. Recite the verse in pairs until you can say it from memory.
3. In pairs, each learner shares a time when he or she did not tell the truth and how it ended.
4. Together, suggest how the lie could have been avoided or corrected.

## Practice
1. Recite Proverbs 12:19.
2. Give two situations in which learners may be tempted to lie.
3. Name two ways of overcoming lies.

## Summary
• Proverbs 12:19: a lie has a short life, but truth lives on forever.
• Lying brings loss of trust, more lies and guilt.
• We overcome lies by owning up and asking God for courage.

### Answers to practice
1. A lie has a short life, but truth lives on forever.
2. Any two: to escape punishment, to get money or things, to look important, to avoid work, out of fear.
3. Any two: think before speaking; remember God sees; own up and say sorry; pray for courage; choose truthful friends; correct a lie you told.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Speaking the truth to one another: Ephesians 4:25

LESSON 3: SPEAKING THE TRUTH TO ONE ANOTHER: EPHESIANS 4:25
===========================================================

## What you will learn
• Read Ephesians 4:25 and explain its message.
• Show a desire to always speak the truth.

Curriculum outcomes: a) state the importance of telling the truth; c) desire to always speak the truth according to Ephesians 4:25

## Introduction
In a family or a class, people depend on one another. If one person lies, everyone is affected. Paul wrote to Christians in Ephesus about this.

## Notes
### Ephesians 4:25
The Good News Bible says:

"No more lying, then! Everyone must tell the truth to his fellow believer, because we are all members together in the body of Christ."

Paul wrote this letter to the Christians in Ephesus. He teaches:
- Christians should stop lying completely.
- Every believer should tell the truth to others.
- The reason is that Christians belong together like parts of one body. The eye, hand and foot need to work together honestly. If one part deceives the others, the whole body suffers.

### Living out Ephesians 4:25
- At home: tell parents the truth about where you have been, how you used money, and whether you have done your chores.
- At school: do your own work in examinations, report truthfully what happened in a quarrel, and admit when you have not done homework.
- With friends: keep promises, do not spread false stories about others, and do not pretend.
- In church: be honest in what you say and do.

### Desiring to speak the truth
A truthful person does not tell the truth only when being watched. He or she wants to be truthful because it pleases God. You can grow this desire by:
- praying every day for a truthful heart;
- thinking about the good results of truth: trust, peace and friendship;
- praising others who tell the truth;
- writing poems and songs about truth.

### A short poem
Truth is a light that shines so bright,
It keeps my heart and my conscience right.
A lie will run but soon will fall,
The truth stands tall for one and all.

## Key words
• fellow believer — another Christian
• body of Christ — all Christians, joined together like parts of one body
• desire — a strong wish

## Activity: Poem on always telling the truth
You will need: Bible, Exercise book, Coloured pencils
1. Read Ephesians 4:25 aloud together.
2. Discuss in groups why Christians are compared to members of one body.
3. Each learner writes a short poem on the importance of always telling the truth.
4. Volunteers recite their poems to the class.

## Practice
1. What does Ephesians 4:25 tell Christians to do?
2. According to Ephesians 4:25, why should believers tell the truth to one another?
3. Give two ways you can be truthful at school.

## Summary
• Ephesians 4:25: no more lying; tell the truth to one another.
• Christians belong together like one body, so they must be honest with each other.
• Pray for a heart that always wants to tell the truth.

### Answers to practice
1. Stop lying and tell the truth to one another.
2. Because they are all members together in the body of Christ.
3. Any two: do your own work in exams; report truthfully what happened; admit when you have not done homework; keep promises.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 4.2 TRUTHFULNESS
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. What is truthfulness?
   A. Telling the truth only when caught
   B. Telling the truth always
   C. Keeping quiet always
   D. Telling small lies

2. Which of these is a benefit of telling the truth?
   A. People stop trusting you
   B. You feel guilty
   C. Others trust you
   D. You need more lies

3. Give two reasons why you should always tell the truth.

4. Complete Proverbs 12:19: "A lie has a short life, but ______."
   A. truth is hard
   B. truth lives on forever
   C. truth is for adults
   D. truth hurts

5. What does Proverbs 12:19 teach about lies?

6. Amina lied that she had done her homework. What is the best thing for her to do now?
   A. Tell another lie
   B. Blame her friend
   C. Own up to the teacher and say sorry
   D. Stay away from school

7. Which Bible verse says Christians must tell the truth because they are members together in the body of Christ?
   A. Proverbs 12:19
   B. Ephesians 4:25
   C. Exodus 20:12
   D. Psalm 125:1

8. Who wrote the letter to the Ephesians?
   A. Peter
   B. Paul
   C. Moses
   D. David

9. How can you grow a desire to always tell the truth?
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 4.2 TRUTHFULNESS
========================================

1. B. Telling the truth always
   Truthfulness is telling the truth always, whatever the results.

2. C. Others trust you
   A truthful person is trusted by others.

3. Any two: God commands it; others trust us; we keep friends; we have peace; innocent people are not punished.
   Truth pleases God and builds good relationships.

4. B. truth lives on forever
   The verse says truth lives on forever.

5. Lies do not last; they are soon found out, but the truth stands forever.
   A lie has a short life.

6. C. Own up to the teacher and say sorry
   Owning up and saying sorry is the way to overcome a lie.

7. B. Ephesians 4:25
   Ephesians 4:25 gives this reason.

8. B. Paul
   Paul wrote the letter to the Christians in Ephesus.

9. Any one: pray for a truthful heart; think about the good results of truth; keep truthful friends; write poems or songs about truth.
   A desire for truth grows through prayer and practice.
